video_title: Automated Sales Dashboard Creation with n8n and Lovable
description: This video demonstrates how to create an automated sales dashboard using two distinct workflows in n8n. The first workflow ingests sales data from incoming emails, parses it with an AI agent (Deepseek R1), and updates a Google Sheet. The second workflow exposes this data via a secure webhook, which is then used by Lovable to build and display a dynamic, real-time sales dashboard with various charts and metrics.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: Hello everyone and welcome to another lesson. I'm very happy to have you here with me today.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: Today we're going to do an exciting sales dashboard.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: So the idea is today we're going to be able to, I mean, all of us, we have income. I mean, most of the people who watch my channel are people who have side income, side streams of income, and they make money on the side.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: And I thought that maybe we can do an automation and tie that up with a lovable interface so we can do a sales dashboard that will give us the current sales, this month sales, past month sales, and also a year overview with pie charts.

annotations.content: Dashboard preview showing sales metrics and charts

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: So, that being said, let's go over first the first workflow, because it's split into two workflows.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: So the first workflow is the workflow that we see in front of us, which is it starts with an email trigger.

annotations.content: n8n workflow canvas with email trigger node

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: So this waits on any email that is coming through your attached account. I have my personal domain account.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: So if you have for example a domain, mine is AI autokit.io. I have info at AI autokit.io, so you can put that in here.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: And what I'm saying is email trigger. So anything that is unseen, any email that I get that is unseen, just give me a notification or trigger this whole workflow, okay?

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: This is the first step. The second step is we will check if the sender is within these domains.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: Because we don't want to have every email processed. We're probably getting sales data from specific emails. For example, Stripe. So whenever we get an email from notification at stripe.com, it will be true and continue to the next check.

annotations.content: If node with domain filter conditions

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: So first, we check is it from the emails that we usually get sales from? And then here we have an or between them, so they don't have to all be true to continue.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: And then the next one would be subject check. Here we're saying if the subject contains sold or sale or payment of, then proceed. The reason is sometimes from Stripe, we don't always get notifications about money. Sometimes we get marketing emails or tax invoices.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: And this is why I have this check. It will check that only the emails that have this in the title.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: And then after both of these are done and it is true, it will go to our AI thinking agent and this agent has Deepseek R1 as the brain and it has a structured output.

annotations.content: AI Agent node configuration with Deepseek R1

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: So basically what we're saying here inside of this agent is we're going to take the subject of the email, whether if the text plain is true, take it, if it's not, take the text.html.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: Then we're saying that you're an expert email analyzer and then we say that you need to output this JSON product amount, date and type. And sources to keep in mind - what's the email source? If it comes from Stripe, it's store related. If it comes from other domain, it's newsletter or affiliate.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: And then of course, I want a structured output. The structure would be product string, price number, date, all of that.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: And then we need to update the database and the database is this one. So I have some mock data here.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: So the database is called sales and it has product, price, type and date. This is all what we need to have the dashboard. And here it will keep on updating with new information as it gets.

annotations.content: Google Sheets with sales data columns

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: So if we can see here, this is a test run that I had before. An email landed in my inbox and it went through true true. The output was template one and then the product, the price was 18, the date gave me the date and the type gave me store exactly as I have it.

annotations.content: Workflow execution output showing parsed data

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: The second workflow is a very interesting one, and this is the one that will keep on updating our dashboard.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: So what this one is, it starts with a webhook and this webhook has a production URL.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: But what's important is that I've put credentials for this. So I can create new credentials.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: And I could have authorization and then I put a long string of text as a password for example and I hit save.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: This will give our webhook a password and authorization. That means no one can access this because it's very important - this is sales data and we don't want anyone to access this except authorized people.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: So you can create your own authorization for your own webhooks. Just as any API has authorization, now you can with a webhook create your own authorization.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: And of course, use the production URL, don't use the test URL. And then in the respond, you should always say respond to webhook node because there's a respond to webhook at the end.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: So when this is triggered, what we do is we go and get the sales information from here. We're saying get me all information from this database. Then we aggregate them into one field, all items into one field, and then we respond with all the items back to the webhook.

annotations.content: Google Sheets read + Aggregate + Respond workflow

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: All right, so now that we have both of our workflows ready to go. This is active, this is active, everything is ready. This will wait for any sales email, it will update our database and this will wait for any calls from our dashboard.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: Now what we want to do is go to Lovable. Here I put a long prompt on what I want exactly for the dashboard. I've done a lot of iterations on it in order to get a single prompt that gets me the dashboard that I want. I've also attached an image that I created so it follows the visual style.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: This whole prompt, you can get it with both of these workflows as JSONs so you can create your own dashboard easily by just importing from file for both of these workflows and then you take the prompt and the picture.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: So obviously we're going to wait for this until it finishes because it's going to take a couple of minutes to get our dashboard finished and running.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: So as you can see, it's still running. I just wanted to give you an update. Once it's over, I'll get back to you guys.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: All right, it just finished. As you can see, we have our dashboard here. Let's see if we can open it in a new tab.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: Now how beautiful is this? We have our sales dashboard. Here our sidebar menu. It has the word sales and comes with a logo. It has the current month sales and gives us a trend from last month. It gives us the last month sales, this year and total sales so far. And here it gives us daily sales by type and the pie chart of divisions by type.

annotations.content: Full sales dashboard with charts and metrics

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: And here it gives us the general pie chart of what are the divisions by type. Now, how beautiful is that?

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: So that was all made from the prompt that we gave it and then the image that we supplied. Let's get back to n8n. This is all taking information from this webhook. If we go to executions, you can see it executed this one and gave the information back - 163 records aggregated and sent back to the webhook.

annotations.content: n8n execution log showing webhook response

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: So for example, if we copy this one and paste it and put a really ridiculous number like $340 and change the date to today's date, wait until it saves, go back and refresh - we should see a change in the dashboard.

annotations.content: Adding new sales record to Google Sheets

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: There you go. As you can see, we made $340 and the whole price changed and here it changed as well.

transcription.speaker: Host
transcription.text: So as you can see, it's a live dashboard that takes information from a live webhook. I hope you guys enjoyed this lesson. I will put everything - both JSONs, the image and the prompt - available inside my community. Please give it a like, subscribe for more videos and see you in the next one.
